title: After AI: where the constraint moves when intelligence leaves the screen

theses.headline: The AI frontier moves from model access to firm-power siting.
theses.needle: Contiguous land, fiber proximity, behind-the-meter firm generation rights, interconnection optionality, cooling, and local permitting bundled into a deployable data-center campus.
theses.metric: Track hyperscaler and data-center developer announcements that name on-site firm power, geothermal, or interconnection bypass as the reason for site selection; count 100 MW plus campuses with direct power-development partnerships; track transformer lead times and local moratoria.
theses.kill: Kill if by end 2028 fewer than two hyperscaler-scale campuses publicly secure behind-the-meter firm clean generation as a core siting advantage, or if transformer and interconnection delays normalize below roughly 24 months in the main US AI data-center markets.
theses.exposed: Hyperscaler infrastructure teams, data-center developers, power developers, large AI labs with reserved compute needs, and investors underwriting AI infrastructure.
theses.action_now: Map sites by firm-power time-to-energize, not just land cost and fiber; secure options on campuses where geothermal, gas with carbon capture, nuclear restart, or other firm power can be contracted behind the meter.
theses.decision_changed: Data-center site selection, PPA strategy, power-development partnerships, capex phasing, and portfolio exposure to grid-dependent versus power-secured data-center assets.
theses.watch: A hyperscaler or top data-center REIT announcing a 100 MW plus campus whose stated differentiator is behind-the-meter clean firm power rather than cheap land.

theses.headline: Physical AI's bottleneck is certified deployment, not robot bodies.
theses.needle: Verified task data, sim-to-real validation, workcell commissioning, safety certification, and field support for physical AI in factories and warehouses.
theses.metric: Track robot OEMs or large integrators selling task libraries, simulation validation, or commissioning layers as separate line items; track public claims of 40 percent plus cuts in commissioning time; track safety certification language in physical-AI deployments.
theses.kill: Kill if by end 2028 humanoid or mobile manipulation deployments scale mainly through turnkey robot hardware with little separate pricing for task validation, commissioning software, or safety case tooling.
theses.exposed: Manufacturing COOs, logistics operators, industrial automation integrators, robot OEMs, and investors in physical AI companies.
theses.action_now: Inventory repeatable tasks by commissioning burden and safety risk; structure pilots around validated productive hours and time-to-commission, not robot count or demo quality.
theses.decision_changed: Automation capex, integrator selection, pilot design, safety certification budgets, and whether to invest in robot OEMs or deployment-layer tooling.
theses.watch: A major automotive or logistics deployment where the press release names the validation, simulation, or task-library layer as the reason the rollout scaled.

theses.headline: Autonomous science shifts the bottleneck from model discovery to experimental throughput.
theses.needle: Robotic experimental throughput with standardized metadata, reliable assays, calibrated uncertainty, and provenance that lets models learn from results without poisoning the loop.
theses.metric: Track DOE and national-lab testbed awards, pharma/materials partnerships that buy autonomous lab capacity, assay throughput per researcher, and publications where the bottleneck is experiment generation rather than model inference.
theses.kill: Kill if by 2029 model-only AI discovery companies repeatedly produce commercially validated materials or therapies without materially expanding wet-lab or physical-test throughput.
theses.exposed: Pharma R&D leaders, materials companies, national labs, AI-for-science founders, and investors underwriting discovery platforms.
theses.action_now: Audit which discovery programs are experiment-limited; secure access to robotic testbeds, assay vendors, and metadata/provenance infrastructure before model-generated proposal volume spikes.
theses.decision_changed: R&D budget allocation between foundation models, lab automation, assay capacity, data infrastructure, and strategic partnerships.
theses.watch: A major pharma, chemicals, or materials company publicly saying its AI discovery bottleneck is lab throughput or assay availability, not model quality.

theses.headline: The consumer AI interface moves to always-on edge devices, gated by thermals, battery, sensors, and privacy.
theses.needle: Low-power NPUs, sensor fusion, local memory, privacy-preserving orchestration, and thermal envelopes for always-on personal AI.
theses.metric: Track commercial devices that run billion-parameter local models, all-day context capture, or private agentic features on wearables/glasses/phones; track battery complaints, thermal throttling, and local AI developer APIs.
theses.kill: Kill if by end 2028 the dominant consumer AI usage remains cloud-chat inside phones and browsers, with wearables and glasses failing to show persistent local context as a major usage mode.
theses.exposed: Device OEMs, chip vendors, mobile OS teams, consumer AI app developers, regulated enterprise buyers, and privacy/security teams.
theses.action_now: Design around local context and power budgets; build features that improve when personal data stays on device instead of depending on generic cloud memory.
theses.decision_changed: Hardware roadmap, NPU vendor selection, app architecture, privacy posture, and whether to build for cloud-first chat or local context surfaces.
theses.watch: A Google, Samsung, Apple, or Meta product launch where the lead AI feature runs persistently on device and is marketed around private context rather than a bigger cloud model.

theses.headline: Biomanufacturing's bottleneck is scale-up, not AI organism design.
theses.needle: Pilot and commercial-scale fermentation, downstream processing, strain robustness, feedstock flexibility, QA systems, and process-development talent.
theses.metric: Track AI-designed or engineered bio-products that fail or delay on COGS and scale-up; track pilot fermentation capacity, downstream bottlenecks, and offtake contracts tied to price parity rather than sustainability premium.
theses.kill: Kill if by 2030 multiple AI-designed industrial bio-products reach commodity-relevant scale and price parity without scarce pilot capacity, downstream processing, or process-development labor becoming a public bottleneck.
theses.exposed: Industrial biotech founders, chemicals strategics, food and materials companies, climate-tech investors, and CDMOs.
theses.action_now: Underwrite AI-bio companies on scale-up evidence, COGS path, downstream process, feedstock contracts, and pilot capacity access before valuing design claims.
theses.decision_changed: Investment diligence, partnership timing, pilot plant capex, CDMO contracting, and whether to buy design IP or process know-how.
theses.watch: A well-funded AI-bio or synbio company delaying launch because pilot capacity, downstream recovery, or COGS fails despite successful lab design.

theses.headline: Agentic AI's scarce layer becomes authority, auditability, and rollback.
theses.needle: Identity, permissioning, tool-access control, audit trails, reversible execution, human authorization policies, and liability evidence for agent actions.
theses.metric: Track enterprise RFPs requiring agent audit logs, least-privilege controls, rollback, or insurance support; track public agent incidents; track vendors selling action-governance rather than generic model monitoring.
theses.kill: Kill if by mid-2028 large enterprises widely deploy multi-step agents with real system authority using mostly prompt-level guardrails and generic logging, without a separate action-governance budget.
theses.exposed: CISOs, CIOs, compliance leaders, insurers, enterprise software buyers, agent platform vendors, and legal teams.
theses.action_now: Design agent deployments around authority boundaries first: least privilege, approval ladders, audit logs, rollback, and evidence packets for regulated workflows.
theses.decision_changed: Enterprise AI procurement, security architecture, insurance underwriting, compliance budgets, and whether agents are allowed to touch systems of record.
theses.watch: A Fortune 500 RFP, insurance policy, or regulator explicitly requiring agent action logs, approval chains, and rollback for production deployment.
